A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DIA-HARM study, with readable main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices. The renamed corpus and relocated appendix material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original transformation-quality measurements, detector evaluations, cross-dialect transfer experiments, error analyses and prompting experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in Sections 4–6 and the appendices, including the prompting and in-context learning experiments.

M1.justification: The Multi-VALUE transformations, D-PURIFY filtering and Feature Accuracy procedure are unchanged. Renaming D3 to D-CUBE and explicitly grouping existing benchmark components do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine source benchmarks, 50 English dialects and human, AI-generated and mixed content scenarios. The five-dialect prompting subset is also retained; D-CUBE is the renamed D3 corpus.

E2.justification: The 16-model main evaluation and three-model appendix prompting comparison retain their comparator sets. Newly cited Chain-of-Interactions and LLM-as-judge work is discussed as future work, not evaluated.

E3.justification: The filtering thresholds, 80/10/10 splits, training configurations, metrics and SQ1–SQ4 procedures remain unchanged. The prompting and exemplar-selection protocols move from v1 Appendix P to v2 Appendix O without substantive revision.

E4.justification: Filtering case studies, training-regime comparisons, abstention analysis, FPR/FNR analysis, qualitative errors and prompting sensitivity experiments are retained. Removing v1’s duplicated FPR/FNR appendix does not remove distinct analysis or evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the across-dialect standard deviations, Figure 4’s 95% confidence intervals and fixed-seed exemplar selection. FPR/FNR entries marked as estimated and pending recomputation retain those qualifications.

E6.justification: Matched main-text and appendix results retain their values and findings. For example, Table 7 preserves RoBERTa’s 87.3, 97.1 and 96.9 F1 scores across training regimes, and Tables 48–49 preserve all prompting and in-context learning results.

T1.justification: The semantic and label-preservation constraints, robustness-gap equation (1), Feature Accuracy equations (2)–(3), and FPR/FNR definitions are unchanged. No new theoretical result or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The benchmark novelty claim, coverage and principal empirical conclusions remain unchanged. The abstract, contributions and conclusion clarify how the existing corpus, validation pipeline and evaluation framework constitute DIA-HARM.

C2.justification: The Ethics Statement adds an interpretation emphasizing potentially severe consequences in resource-constrained settings and long-tail populations. The limitations also specify Chain-of-Interactions and LLM-as-judge approaches as future directions; existing findings and limitations remain.

D1.justification: The resource footnote changes from a repository link to a project website, and new acknowledgments disclose CloudBank computational support. Appendix G’s hardware, training times, hyperparameters and implementation instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Lucas et al. (2025) on Chain-of-Interactions and Gu et al. (2024) on LLM-as-judge to support future directions. The broader positioning is unchanged; duplicated Lucas and Maung 2024 bibliography entries represent existing works, not additional research coverage.

P1.justification: V2 renames D3 to D-CUBE, clarifies benchmark terminology, consolidates v1’s duplicate Appendices M/N into Appendix M, and repairs unresolved cross-references. Author/contact information and acknowledgments also change, while most prose and section organization remain.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, Figure 2’s caption is revised, and extensive appendix reformatting relocates tables, repositions captions and changes table sizes. Several dense tables gain larger text, while Table 29 changes from an upright landscape display to a slightly smaller sideways portrait display. These substantially revise presentation without changing results.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies the benchmark/corpus relationship, removes duplicated analysis, fixes broken cross-references and improves several dense tables’ legibility. These provide a modest readability and navigation gain with unchanged scientific evidence. The smaller sideways transfer matrix and newly duplicated bibliography entries are limited editorial drawbacks.
